601: B is correct because creating an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL instance establishes continuous replication that keeps data synchronized until cutover, and promoting the replica makes it the writable primary of a new Aurora PostgreSQL cluster with only a brief interruption. This achieves minimal downtime and minimal data loss, whereas a snapshot restore or pg_dump approach requires a lengthy offline window and loses any changes made after the backup was taken.
602: C is correct because AWS Backup provides a single managed backup plan that can protect the entire group of EC2 instances, including their attached EBS volumes and instance configuration, without writing any custom automation. Restores of multiple instances can then be initiated through the AWS Backup API or AWS CLI, making both the protection and the recovery of every instance the lowest-effort approach compared to manually managing snapshots per instance.
603: B is correct because the AWS Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode is designed for large-scale parallel processing of up to thousands of items, such as a semistructured dataset in Amazon S3, by spawning a child workflow execution for each item while remaining fully serverless. It provides the most operational efficiency for this workload, since Inline mode is limited to a small number of concurrent iterations and plain Lambda functions would require custom orchestration and scaling code.
604: D is correct because transferring 10 PB over a 500 Mbps uplink, even using 80% of it, would take far longer than the 6-week window, so any network-based option like DataSync, rsync, or the AWS CLI cannot finish in time. Ordering multiple AWS Snowball devices allows the company to copy the data locally at high speed and ship the devices to AWS for import into Amazon S3, which is the purpose-built approach for one-time petabyte-scale migrations.
605: D is correct because a volume gateway configured with cached volumes keeps only frequently accessed data on local on-premises storage for low-latency access while the complete dataset is stored asynchronously in Amazon S3. Because the gateway still presents an iSCSI interface, existing servers continue working with minimal infrastructure changes, and the dependency on on-premises storage hardware is reduced.
606: B is correct because S3 Standard provides high durability and immediate availability for the frequent access expected during the first 30 days, and a lifecycle rule that transitions objects to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days lowers storage costs while preserving millisecond access and multi-AZ resilience. This is the most cost-effective fit, since Glacier classes add retrieval delays that conflict with the requirement that objects be readily available at any time.
607: C is correct because storing the 6 MB document blobs in an Amazon S3 bucket and keeping only object metadata in the existing RDS database offloads blob processing and storage from the database, restoring performance and reducing cost. Amazon S3 is highly available and resilient, making this the most cost-effective design change compared to resizing the instance or migrating to a different database engine.
608: A is correct because associating an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB and using IP set rules allows only the registered retail location IP addresses to reach the application on port 443 while blocking all other traffic. WAF IP sets can be easily updated as registrations change and can hold a very large number of addresses, unlike network ACLs, which would require an impractical number of ingress rules.
609: B is correct because AWS Lake Formation data filters natively implement row-level security and cell-level security on governed tables, restricting access to sensitive rows and columns without any custom code. This built-in capability meets the requirement to prevent access to portions of the data with the least operational overhead compared to building and maintaining Lambda functions to scrub the data.
610: B is correct because a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 routes the EC2-to-S3 traffic over the AWS private network, ensuring the compliance-regulated data never traverses the public internet. An AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and the VPC gives the data center servers a private path to consume the application output, also avoiding the public internet.
611: A is correct because Amazon Kinesis Data Streams durably ingests the near-real-time data and buffers it, decoupling ingestion from processing so that volume spikes no longer overwhelm the application. AWS Lambda functions then consume and process the records in parallel and scale automatically with the stream's throughput, eliminating the 503 errors caused by the compute capacity reaching its limit.
612: D is correct because a VPC endpoint, specifically a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3, provides a private connection from the private subnet to the bucket entirely over the AWS network without an internet gateway or NAT. Updating the S3 bucket policy to allow access only from that endpoint enforces the private path, meeting the requirement that the application not use the internet to reach S3.
613: B is correct because Amazon EKS natively supports enabling envelope encryption of Kubernetes secrets with an AWS KMS key directly on the cluster through a simple configuration change. This built-in option requires no application code changes or custom tooling, making it the least operationally burdensome way to ensure the sensitive information is encrypted.
614: D is correct because an Application Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group is the recommended internal tier-to-tier communication pattern, and security groups are the stateful, instance-level control that can reference the web servers' security group as the allowed source. This configuration ensures only the web servers can access the application servers, whereas network ACLs are stateless and enforce rules at the subnet level.
615: D is correct because Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights is purpose-built to automatically collect, aggregate, and summarize metrics and logs from containerized workloads on Amazon EKS and present them centrally in the CloudWatch console. It delivers cluster, service, and task-level observability for the microservices with minimal setup, whereas the plain agent, App Mesh, or CloudTrail do not provide this aggregated operational view.
616: C is correct because Amazon GuardDuty is an intelligent threat-detection service that continuously monitors the AWS account, workloads, and access patterns, including anomalous access to S3 buckets, for malicious activity. Sending its findings to AWS Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes the suspicious activity and displays it on a dashboard, satisfying the continuous monitoring, reporting, and visualization requirements.
617: B is correct because Amazon EFS is a managed, elastic NFS file system that multiple AWS resources can mount concurrently over the NFS protocol the company already uses. E is correct because installing an AWS DataSync agent on premises and running a DataSync task performs an online migration of the 200 GB of data without interrupting existing services and is more automated and cost-effective than manual copy operations. 618: C is correct because a Multi-AZ deployment type for FSx for Windows File Server maintains a standby file server in a separate Availability Zone with automatic failover, which supports the 5-minute RPO during planned maintenance or unplanned disruptions. Copying backups to us-west-2 fulfills the cross-Region replication requirement, and AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode ensures that no user, including root or administrators, can delete the replicated data for the 5-year minimum retention period, which governance mode would not strictly guarantee.
619: C is correct because a service control policy in AWS Organizations is enforced at the organization level and applies to member accounts regardless of which identity attempts the action, including the account root user. Attaching an SCP that denies changes to CloudTrail to the developer accounts guarantees the mandatory trail configuration cannot be modified, whereas IAM policies attached within the account cannot constrain the root user.
620: C is correct because a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) Amazon EBS volume provides durable, block-level storage with a consistent and predictable low-latency performance backed by an IOPS SLA, which suits a business-critical application. The other storage types either are ephemeral, volatile, or optimized for throughput rather than consistent low-latency random I/O.
